## New Cross-Domain Connections

- **[2026-11-07] Today's Guardian profile of Sheikh Tahnoon puts one name behind an investor that appears twice in AI & Tech's capex pages and nowhere else in the wiki. Neither page treats that investor as a single, politically exposed source of funding.** [[podcasts/podcast-the-guardian-long-read-fixer-financier-spymaster-sheikh-tahnoon]] (added 11-07) describes Tahnoon as the UAE's National Security Adviser and the man who controls MGX, G42, ADQ and ADIA, roughly $1.5tn in all. It also reports a 2026 stake in the holding company behind World Liberty Financial, the Trump family's crypto venture. MGX is already in the wiki in two places: as a named investor in xAI's $20B Series E ([[ai-tech/data-foundation-model-companies-2026-06-27]]) and as the lead partner in Campus AI Paris, Europe's largest planned AI campus (1.4 GW by 2030, since scaled to 3 GW across France; [[ai-tech/data-dc-power-construction-tracker-2026-06-25]]). Both pages list MGX as an ordinary financial backer. The profile says that capital is tied to US–UAE chip-export deals and to one man's political standing, so a change in Nvidia export licensing to the Gulf, or a Washington backlash against the World Liberty link, would hit xAI's funding and the Paris campus's timing together. Crypto also has a gap: [[crypto/defi-watchlist]] and [[finance/investor-letters/source-bond-market-bessent-stablecoins-2026-09-02]] track Tether and Circle as Treasury-buying stablecoins but not World Liberty's, which has a sovereign-linked shareholder. Smallest useful step: add an "ultimate controller / political exposure" note to the MGX rows in both AI & Tech pages, and add World Liberty to the stablecoin list in defi-watchlist with the Tahnoon stake marked "reported, unverified".
- **[2026-11-07] The DC-power model lists Iberdrola only as a generator, the side its own table says faces power prices about 15% lower. Today's Dividend Talk episode says Iberdrola's growth is coming from the other side: regulated networks, which the same model names as the Iberian bottleneck.** [[ai-tech/model-dc-power-regional-balance-2026-06-25]] rates Iberdrola (IBE.MC) "Medium-High" because of its Fernando Pessoa solar farm next to Start Campus Sines. It records about −15% on 2026 forward power prices for the region and concludes that "the constraint is not generation — it is transmission". It then names only REE/Redeia as the transmission play. [[podcasts/podcast-dividend-talk-episode-311-q3-earnings-season]] (added 11-07) reports Iberdrola's Q3: regulated asset base +14% and the interim dividend +8.7%, both driven by grid spending. A regulated network earns its allowed return whatever the power price does, so Iberdrola is a hedged way to own the transmission bottleneck the model identifies, not a generator exposed to falling prices. Iberdrola is on no Finance page, so the DC-power thesis has never been turned into a European position. Next step: from the Q3 2026 results, split Iberdrola's RAB growth by country (Spain vs the UK and US networks), to see how much of it is the Iberian grid bottleneck and how much is unrelated US/UK spending. Then add a networks row to the model's Iberia table, and check whether IBE.MC is in the EU watchlist universe.

_No new investigation ideas, no podcast books (5 new podcast pages scanned, none names a book), no ideas resolved._

## New Cross-Domain Connection

- **[2026-11-06] Fred's Terrain Autobattler already has a working savings rule: +1 gold for every 10 held, up to +3. His Children's Financial Literacy Game stub has had "teach saving and compound interest" as its whole design since May, with no mechanic. The first game already holds a tested mechanic for the second.** [[games/terrain-autobattler-factions-units-economy]] sets income at 5 gold base per round, +1 for each 10 held (max +3) and +1 per PvP win, with no streak gold. Its AI opponents run `greedy`, `balanced` or `aggressive` economy styles. `raw/games/Childrens Financial Literacy Game.md` (listed in [[games/prototypes]]) says the game should teach "saving, spending, earning, compound interest", and its Lightfin todo (coral coins) has been open since 05-01. Two points make the borrowing worth doing, not just noting. (1) The autobattler's interest does compound, because interest gold counts toward the next round's holdings. But the +3 cap means saving past 30 gold earns nothing extra, so the best play is "save up to a target, then spend the surplus". That is a sound budgeting lesson for kids, but it is not how real compound interest works. If the kids' game copies the mechanic, it must decide on purpose whether to keep the cap (budget lesson) or remove it (growth lesson). (2) The game's existing 2,000-fight balance harness ([[games/terrain-autobattler-map-pipeline]], used today for map fairness) runs single fights on fixed boards, not whole matches, so it does not yet test economy. Extended to full AI-vs-AI matches, it could answer with numbers the question a kids' game would try to teach: how often the `greedy` economy beats the `aggressive` one. Smallest next step: when [[games/prototypes]] is filled in, have the financial-literacy row cite the autobattler's income table as its starting mechanic, and record the cap decision there.
